GpuSpec.description: The GPU type and count to rent. Only types listed by `GET /ai/sandbox-gpu-types` are accepted, with a count from their `allowed_counts`; anything else fails with `resources_not_allowed`. Currently each type lists one count, so the sandbox gets a whole node of that type.

count.description: A count from the type's `allowed_counts`. Currently that's the node's GPU count, so the sandbox rents a whole node.

ImageSpec.description: The container image to run. The image must be publicly pullable and have a `linux/amd64` variant.

ref.description: Image reference, e.g. `ghcr.io/acme/trainer:1.4`. The image must be publicly pullable and have a `linux/amd64` variant. The registry must be a public DNS name; IP literals, `localhost`, single-label hosts and internal registries fail with `registry_not_allowed`.

LogsIncompleteReason.description:
Why some of the sandbox's output is permanently missing from the archive:
`log_bucket_unavailable` (the log bucket couldn't be written), `node_lost` (the
sandbox's node was lost), `logs_missing` (output was lost on its way to the
archive), `logs_unverified` (the sandbox's output couldn't be counted, so the
archive can't be shown complete), or `size_cap_reached` (the output passed the
size cap).

NetworkMode.description: Outbound network access, fixed at create: `public` (the internet, never internal addresses), `blocked` (`block_network: true`; no network at all, not even DNS) or `allowlist` (`cidr_allowlist`; only those CIDRs).

ReadinessProbe.description: How to tell the sandbox is ready; drives the `ready` field. Set exactly one of `tcp_port` or `exec`; the other may be omitted or `null`.

exec.description: Not set for a TCP port probe.

tcp_port.description: Ready once this port accepts connections inside the sandbox.

exec.description: Ready once this command (argv) exits with 0.

tcp_port.description: Not set for an exec probe.

ResolvedSpec.description:
What actually runs, resolved before the sandbox is placed. Set once the image
is resolved.

Sandbox.description: A sandbox: one container image running in its own virtual machine. Terminated sandboxes stay readable for at least 30 days.

cpu.description: CPU cores: the GPU type's per-GPU default × the GPU count.

disk_gib.description: Size in GiB of `/data`, the sandbox's own disk: the GPU type's per-GPU default × the GPU count. Writing past it fails with "no space left on device", and the sandbox keeps running. Everything written outside `/data` counts against the root filesystem's separate limit (`root_disk_gib` in the GPU types list); going past that ends the sandbox with `disk_limit_exceeded`.

exit_code.description: The main process's exit code; set whenever it ran.

gpu.description: The rented GPU type and count.

idle_timeout.description: Idle timeout in seconds, if set.

log_bucket.description: The bucket the sandbox's logs go to, the bucket created for you included; `null` until it's known.

logs_incomplete.description: Some output is permanently missing from the archive.

memory_mib.description: Memory in MiB: the GPU type's per-GPU default × the GPU count.

ready.description: Whether the readiness probe passes. Without a probe, `true` once `running`.

resolved.description: Set once the image is resolved and the working directory is known.

termination_message.description: Why the sandbox ended, when there's more to say than `termination_reason`. Set in two cases only. With `image_pull_failed`, before the sandbox ran: the registry's own message, or what Telnyx's checks of the image found (the reference, the image's platform, ENTRYPOINT/CMD, WorkingDir or User). Text from your registry is shown as received, cleaned of control characters. With `internal_error`: a short reason from Telnyx, such as the sandbox's disk not being ready.

timeout.description: Maximum lifetime in seconds; `null` means no limit.

SandboxCreateReq.description: A new sandbox. `image` and `gpu` are required.

not.description: `block_network: true` can't be combined with a `cidr_allowlist`.

block_network.description: No network at all, not even DNS (network mode `blocked`). Can't be combined with `cidr_allowlist`.

cidr_allowlist.description: Allow outbound traffic only to these CIDRs (network mode `allowlist`). Internal address ranges are always excluded; a CIDR entirely inside them fails with `cidr_not_allowed`. DNS isn't included: allow your resolver's addresses, or connect by IP. Can't be combined with `block_network`.

command.description: Full argv to run, replacing the image's ENTRYPOINT and CMD. Omit it to run the image's own ENTRYPOINT + CMD; if the image has neither, the sandbox ends with `termination_reason: no_command`.

env.description: Environment variables, on top of the image's. Names must be POSIX names and can't start with `TELNYX_SANDBOX_`; at most 256 variables, 32 KiB each and 256 KiB in total (else `invalid_env`).

gpu.description: The GPU type and a count from its `allowed_counts`, as listed by `GET /ai/sandbox-gpu-types`. Currently that's the node's GPU count, so the sandbox gets a whole node of that type, with the type's CPU, memory and disk.

idle_timeout.description: End the sandbox (reason `idle_timeout`) after this many seconds of no activity. Activity is an exec running, starting or finishing, and stdin written to an exec or to the main process. Reading output doesn't count, nor do file calls (reading, writing, listing or deleting files), nor does the main process's own work: a sandbox whose main process is a server, with nothing else going on, ends after `idle_timeout`. Must not exceed `timeout` when that is a number. Default: none.

log_bucket.description: Your own Cloud Storage bucket for this sandbox's logs. It must exist, belong to your organization, be in the Cloud Storage region this service keeps sandbox logs in, and be writable; otherwise the create fails with `log_bucket_not_allowed`. Omit it to use a bucket created for you in your account, with a 30-day lifecycle rule; the sandbox waits for that bucket before it waits for capacity.

name.description: Optional name, unique among your non-terminated sandboxes (else `name_conflict`); reusable once the sandbox holding it is terminated. Look it up with `GET /ai/sandboxes?name=…`.

queue_timeout.description: How long to wait before placement, in seconds: resolving the image, waiting for capacity and preparing GPUs all count. Then the sandbox ends with `queue_timeout`, so with `0` it always does. Queued and preparing time isn't billed.

readiness_probe.description: How to tell the sandbox is ready (see `ready`).

tags.description: Your own key/value labels, e.g. `{"project": "llm-ft"}`. At most 20 tags; keys 1–63 characters, values up to 255. Filter on them with `GET /ai/sandboxes?tag[<key>]=<value>`.

timeout.description: Maximum lifetime in seconds. Omitted: 300 s. `null`: no limit; the sandbox runs until it's terminated. There's no maximum. Send an explicit `null` for no limit: a client that drops null fields gets the 300 s default.

workdir.description: Absolute working directory (else `invalid_workdir`). Defaults to the image's WorkingDir, then `/`. Execs default to it too.

SandboxState.description:
Lifecycle state: `queued` → `preparing` (GPU preparation, when needed) →
`scheduled` → `starting` (pulling the image) → `running` → `terminated`.
Any non-terminal state can go straight to `terminated`, which is final.

SandboxUpdateReq.description: New tags for a sandbox. Nothing else can change after create.

tags.description: Replaces the whole tag set; `{}` clears it. Your own key/value labels, e.g. `{"project": "llm-ft"}`. At most 20 tags; keys 1–63 characters, values up to 255. Filter on them with `GET /ai/sandboxes?tag[<key>]=<value>`.

url.description: Documentation page for the error code.

TelnyxErrorSource.description: Where in the request the error was found.

pointer.description: JSON pointer into the request body, e.g. `/timeout`.

TerminationReason.description:
Why the sandbox ended. Always set once `state` is `terminated`.

- Before running: `queue_timeout`, `terminated_by_user` (cancelled while queued), `image_pull_failed` (the image can't be used; `termination_message` says why when it's known), `no_command` (the image has no ENTRYPOINT or CMD and no `command` was given), `account_suspended`, `killed_by_operator`, `spend_limit_reached`, `internal_error`.
- From running: `exit` (see `exit_code`), `timeout`, `idle_timeout`, `terminated_by_user`, `oom_killed`, `disk_limit_exceeded`, `account_suspended`, `killed_by_operator`, `spend_limit_reached`, `node_lost`, `internal_error`.

`spend_limit_reached`: your account, or the API key that created the sandbox, reached its Sandboxes spend limit. A sandbox ended this way isn't restarted when the limit is raised.

total_results.description: Number of items across all pages.

sandboxes_TelnyxError.description: One error in the standard Telnyx error body.

code.description: Telnyx error code: a 5-digit string for general errors, e.g. `10009`. Sandboxes-specific errors are identified by their name in `title`.

title.description: Short, constant summary of the error. For Sandboxes-specific errors, the error's name, e.g. `quota_exceeded`.

BearerAuth.description: Telnyx API key supplied as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. In production, auth may be validated by the API gateway and forwarded via Telnyx auth headers.

Payment.description: Machine Payment Protocol credential used on paid retries, sent as `Authorization: Payment ...`. Obtained by paying a challenge returned in the `WWW-Authenticate` header of a 402 response. This is not a Telnyx API key; initial challenge requests use standard bearer authentication instead.
Payment.name: Authorization

collections_bearerAuth.description: Telnyx API key. Collections and results are automatically scoped to the authenticated user's organization.

number-reputation_bearerAuth.description: Telnyx API key. Generate one at https://portal.telnyx.com/#/app/api-keys.

pronunciation-dicts_bearerAuth.description: Telnyx API v2 key. Obtain from https://portal.telnyx.com

Terminated sandboxes stay readable for at least 30 days.

post.description:
Creates a sandbox and returns it at once in state `queued`. It then starts in the background (`queued` → `preparing`, when its GPUs need preparing → `scheduled` → `starting` → `running`); follow it with `GET /ai/sandboxes/{sandbox_id}`, or wait for it to end with `GET /ai/sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/wait`.

Set `gpu` to a type and a count from its `allowed_counts`, as listed by `GET /ai/sandbox-gpu-types`. Currently each type lists one count, its node's GPU count, so a sandbox rents a whole GPU node. Its CPU, memory and disk come from the type.

Defaults: `timeout` 300 s (send `null` for no limit), `queue_timeout` 600 s, network mode `public`.

When there's no capacity, the sandbox waits in the queue for up to `queue_timeout`; queued and preparing time isn't billed. A create that would take your organization over its GPU limit for the type fails at once with `quota_exceeded`; contact support to raise the limit.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`: if the response is lost, a retry with the same key returns the same sandbox instead of starting (and billing) a second one.

parameters.description: Optional client-chosen key (e.g. a UUID, at most 255 characters) that makes the call safe to retry. Within 24 h, the same key with the same request returns the stored response instead of acting twice; the same key with a different request fails with `idempotency_key_reused`; a request with a key that's still being processed fails with `request_in_progress`.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

post.description:
Stops the sandbox. A queued or preparing sandbox is cancelled at once. A sandbox that has been placed is stopped asynchronously: its processes get `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` if they're still running after a grace period, and it reaches `terminated` with `termination_reason: terminated_by_user` and the main process's `exit_code` if it ran. The response shows the sandbox as it is now; use `GET /ai/sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/wait` to see it end.

If the sandbox already ended on its own, its own reason stays. Terminating a terminated sandbox succeeds and changes nothing.

parameters.description: Optional client-chosen key (e.g. a UUID, at most 255 characters) that makes the call safe to retry. Within 24 h, the same key with the same request returns the stored response instead of acting twice; the same key with a different request fails with `idempotency_key_reused`; a request with a key that's still being processed fails with `request_in_progress`.
